diagnosis_explanation:
Your kidneys are not working well enough. This is called end-stage renal disease. You are getting dialysis treatments. This helps clean your blood.

You also have trouble with your heart. It is not pumping blood as strongly as it should. This is called congestive heart failure. Your diabetes can also affect your body. It can lead to other problems. You have low blood platelet counts. This means you have less blood than is normal. Your body is also not getting enough nutrients. This is protein malnourishment. You also had a broken bone in your back. This was a T9 vertebral fracture. You also had an infection in the disc in your spine. This is called diskitis.
medication_rationale: Your doctor did not give you any new medicines to take at home. Ask at your next visit if you need to start any.
recovery_trajectory:
**Week 1:**
- You might feel tired from treatment this week.
- You can move around your home slowly.
- You can eat more food now.
- You should drink plenty of fluids.
- Call your doctor if you feel confused or very sleepy.
- Your goal this week is to walk short distances inside.

**Week 2:**
- You may have more energy as the week goes on.
- You can do light tasks around the house.
- Do not lift anything heavy.
- You can eat more foods now.
- Continue drinking plenty of fluids.
- Call your doctor if you have trouble breathing.
- Your goal this week is to walk a little longer each day.

**Week 3:**
- You should feel more like yourself this week.
- You can do more light activities.
- Avoid lifting anything heavy or very hard work.
- Keep eating well and drinking fluids.
- Call your doctor if you have a fast heartbeat.
- Your goal this week is to walk for 15 minutes outside.

**Week 4:**
- You will likely feel much better this week.
- You can go back to many normal activities.
- Talk to your doctor about returning to work.
- Continue eating and drinking well.
- Call your doctor if you have no appetite.
- Your goal this week is to walk daily for 20 minutes.

**When to expect improvement:**
- Your body needs time to recover.
- Keep attending your dialysis treatments.
- Eat healthy foods and drink your fluids.
- Talk to your care team about any worries.
- You will likely feel stronger over the next few weeks.
escalation_guide:
CALL 911 IMMEDIATELY
These symptoms are life-threatening. Do not drive yourself.
- Shortness of breath: Your body needs oxygen now.
- Chest pain: Your heart needs help now.
- Fast heart rate: Call 911 if it is over 100.
- Feeling faint or passing out: Your brain is not getting blood.
- Severe pain: Get help right away.
- Bleeding that will not stop: Apply pressure and call 911.
- Confusion or acting strange: You may have had a stroke.
- Seizure: You lost control of your body.

GO TO THE ER TODAY
Do not wait until tomorrow. Go within a few hours.
- Fever over 101 degrees: You may have an infection.
- Vomiting for 12 hours: You cannot keep any fluids down.
- Wound red streaks or pus: Infection can spread fast.
- Swelling in one leg: This could be a blood clot.
- Sudden weight gain of 2 pounds: Fluid may be building up.
- New confusion getting worse: You may have an infection.
- Fall with injury: Get checked out today.

CALL YOUR DOCTOR
Call during office hours. Do not go to the ER for these.
- No symptoms in this tier for your diagnosis.
